summary.short: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 establishes the European Health Data Space. It grants natural persons access, download, transfer and restriction rights, requires Member States to set up access services and digital health authorities, creates the MyHealth@EU cross-border infrastructure and sets rules for secondary use. Applies from 26 March 2027.
summary.long: Regulation (EU) 2025/327 establishes the European Health Data Space (EHDS) for primary use (healthcare delivery) and secondary use (research, policymaking and related purposes) of electronic health data. The text provided covers Chapter I (general provisions and definitions) and Chapter II, Sections 1 to 3 (rights of natural persons, access by health professionals, priority data categories, digital health authorities and MyHealth@EU). Natural persons may access their priority-category data through electronic health data access services, download copies, insert information, request rectification, transmit data to providers, restrict access and obtain information on accesses. Member States must establish access services and proxy services and designate digital health authorities and national contact points for digital health. Member States may provide an opt-out from access and may delay access for patient-safety reasons. The Commission adopts implementing acts on formats and specifications and establishes MyHealth@EU. Digital health authorities publish biennial activity reports, and complaints go to digital health authorities or supervisory authorities, which may impose administrative fines under Regulation (EU) 2016/679. The recitals also describe the EHR system conformity regime, wellness application labelling, secondary use through health data access bodies and secure processing environments, HealthData@EU and penalties; these chapters are not in the text provided. The regulation applies from 26 March 2027 (Recital 115).

notes: Part 1 of 2 covers the recitals (1) to (115) and Articles 1 to 23 (Chapter I; Chapter II, Sections 1 to 3). Relations and entities are limited to this part; Article 24 onward and the annexes are in part 2. The title says the Regulation amends Directive 2011/24/EU and Regulation (EU) 2024/2847, but the amending provisions are not in part 1. Recitals are context only. The application date 26 March 2027 appears in recital 115 and in deadlines in Articles 13(4), 15(1), 19(1) and 23(2); the general application article is outside part 1. Target instrument IDs are left null because no registry IDs were supplied. Part 2 covers Article 24 to Annex IV. Only relations, entities and notes are coded here. target_instrument_id is empty for all relations because registry IDs for cited acts were not supplied; target_text gives the citation. No enabling legal basis clause appears in this part. Article 105 staggers application: general application from 26 March 2027, Chapter IV from 26 March 2029 with listed exceptions, and Chapter III for EHR systems under Article 26(2) from 26 March 2031. Article 97(2) confers delegated powers for an indeterminate period from 25 March 2025. Notification deadlines differ between Art. 64(8) (26 March 2029) and Art. 99 (26 March 2027); these concern different rules and are not a conflict.

‘personal electronic health data’ means data concerning health and genetic data, processed in an electronic form;
‘non-personal electronic health data’ means electronic health data other than personal electronic health data
‘electronic health data’ means personal or non-personal electronic health data;
‘primary use’ means the processing of electronic health data for the provision of healthcare, in order to assess, maintain or restore the state of health
‘secondary use’ means the processing of electronic health data for the purposes set out in Chapter IV of this Regulation, other than the initial purposes for which they were collected or produced;
‘registration of electronic health data’ means the recording of health data in an electronic format
‘electronic health data access service’ means an online service, such as a portal or an application for mobile devices, that enables natural persons not acting in a professional capacity
‘health professional access service’ means a service, supported by an EHR system, that enables health professionals to access data of natural persons under their treatment
‘electronic health record’ or ‘EHR’ means a collection of electronic health data related to a natural person
‘electronic health record system’ or ‘EHR system’ means any system whereby the software, or a combination of the hardware and the software of that system, allows personal electronic health data
‘putting into service’ means the first use, for its intended purpose, in the Union of an EHR system covered by this Regulation

‘serious incident’ means any malfunction or deterioration in the characteristics or performance of an EHR system made available on the market
‘care’ means a professional service the purpose of which is to address the specific needs of a natural person
‘health data holder’ means any natural or legal person, public authority, agency or other body in the healthcare or the care sectors, including reimbursement services

‘health data user’ means a natural or legal person, including Union institutions, bodies, offices or agencies, which has been granted lawful access to electronic health data for secondary use pursuant to a data permit
‘data permit’ means an administrative decision issued to a health data user by a health data access body to process certain electronic health data
‘dataset’ means a structured collection of electronic health data;

obligations.summary: Annex III: technical documentation contains at least a detailed description of the EHR system, common specifications references, verification test results, the information sheet and the EU declaration of conformity.

evidence.quote: The technical documentation referred to in Article 37 shall contain at least the following information

enforcement.triggered_by: Infringements in monitoring and enforcement of Articles 3 and 5 to 10 of this Regulation (natural persons' rights in primary use)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: up to the amount referred to in Article 83(5) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

evidence.quote: Supervisory authorities shall be empowered to impose administrative fines up to the amount referred to in Article 83(5) of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

enforcement.triggered_by: non-compliance by a health data user with the requirements of Chapter IV (Art. 63(2)-(3))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: revocation of the data permit and stop of the affected processing operation; no monetary maximum stated
enforcement.cure_period: Art. 63(2): notice of findings and opportunity to state views within a reasonable period not exceeding four weeks; no cure period for the revocation stated

evidence.quote: shall have the power to revoke the data permit issued pursuant to Article 68 and stop without undue delay the affected electronic health data processing operation carried out by the health data user

enforcement.triggered_by: non-compliance by a health data user with the requirements of Chapter IV (Art. 63(3))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: exclusion from any access to electronic health data within the EHDS for secondary use for a period of up to five years (may be imposed where appropriate, in accordance with national law)
enforcement.cure_period: Art. 63(2): opportunity to state views within a reasonable period not exceeding four weeks; no cure period stated

evidence.quote: the health data user concerned from any access to electronic health data within the EHDS in the context of secondary use for a period of up to five years

enforcement.triggered_by: health data holder withholds electronic health data with the manifest intention of obstructing its use, or does not respect the deadlines in Art. 60(2)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: periodic penalty payment for each day of delay, transparent and proportionate; amount established by the health data access body in accordance with national law
enforcement.penalty_formula: per day of delay; amount set by the health data access body under national law
enforcement.cure_period: Art. 63(2): opportunity to state views within a reasonable period not exceeding four weeks; no cure period stated

evidence.quote: the health data access body shall have the power to fine the health data holder for each day of delay with a periodic penalty payment, which shall be transparent and proportionate

enforcement.triggered_by: repeated breaches by the health data holder of the obligation of cooperation with the health data access body (Art. 63(4))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: exclusion from submitting health data access applications pursuant to Chapter IV for a period of up to five years (in accordance with national law); holder remains obliged to make data accessible during the exclusion where applicable
enforcement.cure_period: Art. 63(2): opportunity to state views within a reasonable period not exceeding four weeks; no cure period stated

evidence.quote: the health data holder concerned from submitting health data access applications pursuant to this Chapter for a period of up to five years

enforcement.triggered_by: infringements of the duties of health data holders or health data users under Art. 60 and Art. 61(1), (5) and (6)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: maximum of EUR 10 000 000 or, in the case of an undertaking, a maximum of 2 % of total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher
enforcement.penalty_formula: undertaking: 2% of total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher; where several provisions are infringed for the same or a linked data permit or request, total fine capped at the amount for the most serious infringement (Art. 64(3))

evidence.quote: shall be subject to administrative fines of a maximum of EUR 10 000 000 or, in the case of an undertaking, of a maximum of 2 % of its total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

enforcement.triggered_by: health data users processing data for uses prohibited by Art. 54, extracting personal data from secure processing environments, re-identifying or attempting to re-identify natural persons, or not complying with enforcement measures under Art. 63(3) and (4)
enforcement.max_penalty_text: maximum of EUR 20 000 000 or, in the case of an undertaking, a maximum of 4 % of total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher
enforcement.penalty_formula: undertaking: 4% of total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher; where several provisions are infringed for the same or a linked data permit or request, total fine capped at the amount for the most serious infringement (Art. 64(3))

evidence.quote: shall be subject to administrative fines of a maximum of EUR 20 000 000 or, in the case of an undertaking, of a maximum of 4 % of its total worldwide annual turnover in the preceding financial year, whichever is higher

enforcement.triggered_by: infringements of the right to opt out from processing of personal electronic health data for secondary use (Art. 71), which these authorities monitor and enforce
enforcement.max_penalty_text: administrative fines up to the amount referred to in Article 83 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679

evidence.quote: Those supervisory authorities shall be empowered to impose administrative fines up to the amount referred to in Article 83 of Regulation (EU) 2016/679.

enforcement.triggered_by: infringements of this Regulation which are not subject to administrative fines under Art. 63 and Art. 64
enforcement.max_penalty_text: penalties to be laid down by Member States; no amount stated in this text; penalties to be effective, proportionate and dissuasive

evidence.quote: Member States shall lay down the rules on penalties applicable to infringements of this Regulation, in particular for infringements which are not subject to administrative fines pursuant to Articles 63 and 64

enforcement.authority: none designated in this text; claim is made under Union and national law
enforcement.triggered_by: material or non-material damage suffered as a result of an infringement of this Regulation
enforcement.max_penalty_text: right to receive compensation in accordance with Union and national law; no amount stated

evidence.quote: shall have the right to receive compensation in accordance with Union and national law

enforcement.authority: market surveillance authority of the Member State
enforcement.triggered_by: manufacturer or other economic operator fails to cooperate with the market surveillance authority, or provided information or documentation that is incomplete or incorrect (Art. 43(5))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: measures to prohibit or restrict the EHR system from being made available on the market, or to recall or withdraw it; no monetary maximum stated
enforcement.cure_period: measures apply until the manufacturer or economic operator cooperates or provides complete and correct information

evidence.quote: the market surveillance authority may take all appropriate measures to prohibit or restrict the relevant EHR system from being made available on the market

enforcement.authority: market surveillance authorities of the Member States
enforcement.triggered_by: no adequate corrective action taken within a reasonable period after a finding of non-compliance (Art. 45(2)); or persistence of the non-compliance (Art. 45(5))
enforcement.max_penalty_text: provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the EHR system from being made available on the market, or to recall or withdraw it; no monetary maximum stated
enforcement.cure_period: corrective action to be taken by a specific deadline set by the market surveillance authority (Art. 45(1)); no further period stated

evidence.quote: shall take all appropriate provisional measures to prohibit or restrict the EHR system from being made available on the market of their Member States

enforcement.authority: Commission and Member States' market surveillance authorities
enforcement.triggered_by: Commission considers a national measure justified under the Union safeguard procedure (Art. 46(1)) in respect of a non-compliant EHR system
enforcement.max_penalty_text: Member States concerned must withdraw the non-compliant EHR system from their market; no monetary maximum stated

evidence.quote: all Member States concerned shall take the necessary measures to ensure that the non-compliant EHR system is withdrawn from their market
